title: Rav Tavyomi
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He speaks in Abaye’s name: [Kiddushin 14b](https://www.sefaria.org/Kiddushin.14b.12) and [Bava Metzia 54b](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Metzia.54b.7). He and Rav Kahana give differing reports in Rava’s name, as in [Bava Kamma 41b](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Kamma.41b.15). We likewise find in [Eruvin 26b](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.26b.8) and [Zevachim 46b](https://www.sefaria.org/Zevachim.46b.7): “The source abbreviation ר״ב teaches it this way, and Rav Tavyomi teaches it this way.” In [Sanhedrin 97a](https://www.sefaria.org/Sanhedrin.97a.6), Hyman identifies Tavyomi, according to one version, as the one who told Ravina that “if they gave me all the space in the world, I would not alter my words,” etc.; he came before Rava, etc. In [Kiddushin 52a](https://www.sefaria.org/Kiddushin.52a.3): “Tavyomi recited [a baraita].”[^2]

notes.text: The supplied ר״ב remains literal, not an assumed Rav B. identity. Saved Davidson Eruvin 26b and Zevachim 46b both fully write Rav Kahana in the parallel recensions. This is a witness comparison, not printed-letter history or authority binding.

Kiddushin 14b and Bava Metzia give Abaye as Tavyomi’s authority. Eruvin and Zevachim name Rav Kahana in the contrasting recension. Sanhedrin gives Tavyomi as one version of the speaker’s name. In the consulted Sanhedrin passage Rava introduces the story, and Rav Tavot or Rav Tavyomi tells it to him. Hyman’s account gives Ravina as the listener.
